subject: SLA credit floor & batched-inference exception request — Helix Data Systems
messages:
From: Natalie Moore <natalie.moore@helixdata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anil Patel <apatel@helixdata.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template + credit floor + batched inference carveout

Ben —

Thanks for taking this. Quick context: Helix is planning to move our inference-heavy scoring pipeline onto Redwood for the July pilot. Our procurement team needs a working SLA and a clear monthly-credit calculation for our legal review. Two asks up front:

1) Can Redwood support a 99.9% hosted uptime commitment for our workload (we understand high-speed low-latency traffic may be 99.95 by default) — if not, what is the equivalent credit schedule?

2) We run large nightly batched inference windows (non-interactive) that produce sustained token throughput. Can we get a temporary exception for those jobs (first 90 days) where the uptime floor is relaxed with a defined carveout and a capped monthly credit? We need the cap so our finance team can forecast downside risk (they prefer a fixed monthly-credit floor).

Attached: Helix_SLA_RFI.pdf (our procurement checklist) and a monthly usage workbook. We also want to understand scheduled maintenance windows, regional failover, and how credits are calculated if Helix is impacted by degraded regional performance.

Timeline: legal would like a draft SLA by end of week (this Friday). Could you confirm availability for a 30-min sync?

Best,
Natalie
Natalie Moore
Sr. Procurement Manager — Helix Data Systems
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Moore <natalie.moore@helixdata.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template + credit floor + batched inference carveout

Natalie —

Thanks for the clear note and the attachments. High level answers and a proposed starting point below; I attached a short Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v1.docx with the same content for legal redlines.

Uptime baseline
- Redwood hosted default: 99.95% monthly availability for API endpoints (applies to interactive/low-latency routes).
- For your request, we can offer a 99.9% hosted uptime floor for the batch-heavy route (temporary, first 90 days) with an explicit credit cap to limit downside. After pilot we’ll re-evaluate based on observed telemetry.

Monthly credit calculation (proposed)
- If monthly availability >= 99.95%: no credits.
- If monthly availability between 99.9% and 99.95%: credit = 10% of monthly Redwood invoice for impacted route.
- If monthly availability between 99.0% and 99.9%: credit = 25% of monthly Redwood invoice for impacted route.
- If monthly availability < 99.0%: credit = 50% of monthly Redwood invoice for impacted route, capped at 20% of total monthly invoice (this is the credit floor cap Helix requested).

Maintenance & carveouts
- Scheduled maintenance: up to 6 hours per month per region for planned maintenance (we notify 72 hours in advance) is excluded from availability calculations.
- Emergency maintenance/mitigation: brief emergency patches may be applied; we exclude the documented incident windows if documented in our status history.

Regional failover
- We’ll enable cross-region routing for critical endpoints in the pilot. If Helix opts in, requests will route to the nearest healthy region automatically; the SLA applies to the primary region unless you opt into cross-region redundancy (we can add that as an add-on).

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v1.docx includes the above plus definitions (measurement method p95/p99, measurement window UTC, and sample credit calculation).

Next steps
- 30-min sync: I have availability Tue 22 June 10:00–10:30 PT or Tue 22 14:00–14:30 PT. Which works?
- If you’re comfortable, I’ll loop in Connor (legal) and Laura (AM) on the call to accelerate redlines.

Thanks — we’re eager to get Helix into pilot.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Natalie Moore <natalie.moore@helixdata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anil Patel <apatel@helixdata.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template + credit floor + batched inference carveout

Ben —

Appreciate the fast reply and the proposed banding. A few clarifications before the call: 

1) Credit floor cap: Helix’s legal wants the cap to be expressed as a fixed dollar floor (not a percentage cap of the invoice), e.g., no more than $25k per month in credits for the pilot. Is that something Redwood can commit to for the initial 90-day exception?

2) Measurement: you referenced the measurement window — we need the exact metric and measurement points. Are you using internal edge telemetry or a public status feed? We need a reproducible calculation for disputes.

3) Burst/batched carveout: when we say batched inference jobs, we mean sustained token pushes between 01:00–05:00 PT daily that can exceed typical p95-lengths. If those jobs are causing transient backpressure, would Redwood prefer we move those jobs to a dedicated capacity reservation (costing extra) instead of an SLA exception? Please advise recommended path for predictability.

4) Compliance evidence: we also need SOC2 and an uptime history for the last 12 months for your hosted API (applies to our security review). Is SOC2 latest report available?

If you can confirm these points by noon PT, we can take the draft to legal quickly. We’ll take Tue 22 10:00 PT for the call.

Thanks,
Natalie
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Moore <natalie.moore@helixdata.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template + credit floor + batched inference carveout

Natalie —

Great, thanks — confirming the call at Tue 22 Jun 10:00 PT (I’ll send a calendar invite to your team). Answers inline below and summary next steps.

1) Fixed-dollar cap: yes, for the initial 90-day pilot Redwood can agree to a fixed credit ceiling of $25,000/month for the affected batch route. We will document that as a temporary amendment in the SLA. After the pilot, credits revert to the standard percentage-based banding unless otherwise negotiated.

2) Measurement & dispute resolution: availability is calculated from Redwood’s synthetic health checks at the regional ingress (measurement points) and corroborated with request success/failure rates from the API gateway. The SLA doc defines the exact measurement queries (HTTP 200 success over 5-minute buckets) and the calculation formula (total successful requests / total attempted requests for the measurement window). We also keep a public status history and will provide an export for disputes. That will be included in the Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v1.docx and the SOC2 link I’ll share in the call.

3) Burst/batched jobs recommendation: two paths —
- Option A (recommended for predictability): migrate nightly batched jobs to a Dedicated reservation (pointer: Redwood Dedicated) — this guarantees capacity and keeps the hosted API SLA intact. Pricing is a fixed monthly reservation and we can size for your peak windows.
- Option B: keep them on hosted with the temporary 90-day exception and the $25k cap. We’ll also configure separate routes so crediting only applies to the impacted route.

My recommendation is Option A if Helix wants predictable latency and no SLA carveouts long term. For the pilot, Option B plus the fixed-dollar cap is a reasonable compromise.

4) Compliance evidence: SOC2 Type II for 2026–2027 is available. Public link: https://drive.redwood.ai/reports/SOC2-Redwood-2027.pdf. I’ve also shared a one-page uptime summary (last 12 months) in the Drive folder and will bring a CSV to the call if you want to walk through it.

Next steps
- Calendar invite: sent for Tue 22 Jun 10:00–10:30 PT (invite includes Connor and Laura).
- I’ll circulate a short amendment (SLA Pilot Exhibit) capturing: 99.9% pilot floor for batch route, $25k monthly credit ceiling, measurement method, maintenance carveouts, and 90-day sunset. Connor will help incorporate any legal redlines.
- DocuSign: I’ve started a draft envelope for the pilot amendment: https://docusign.com/helix-redwood/sla-redlines/HLX-2027-451 — we’ll not sign until both sides confirm redlines.

If anything else you want in the packet before the call, let me know.

—
